sections.label: McKinsey report on R&D spending
sections.summary: A January 2019 McKinsey report found capitalised spending on R&D and intangible assets grew from 5.4% of revenue in 2000 to 13.1% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A McKinsey Report in January 2019, titled “Globalization in Transition: The Future of Trade and Value Chains”, found that capitalised spending on research and development (R&D) and intangible assets, such as brands, software, and IP, is growing as a share of revenue, from 5.4% in 2000 to 13.1% in 2016.

sections.label: Patent applications in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, there was a total of 11,845 patent applications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In 2018, there was a total of 11,845 patent applications.

sections.label: Claim resolution times and IP consolidation
sections.summary: The 2019 World Bank survey noted Singapore resolves claims in 164 days versus 370 in New York and 437 in London, and most civil IP disputes are being consolidated in the High Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In the latest 2019 World Bank Doing Business Survey, it was noted that it takes 164 days to resolve a claim in Singapore, compared to 370 days in New York and 437 days in London.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, we are consolidating most of the civil IP disputes to be heard in the High Court.

sections.label: High Court exclusive copyright forum
sections.summary: Clause 4 makes the High Court the exclusive forum to hear civil proceedings for most copyright matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 4 makes the High Court the exclusive forum to hear civil proceedings for most copyright matters.

sections.label: High Court exclusive IP jurisdiction
sections.summary: The High Court will have exclusive jurisdiction over civil infringement of copyright and registrable IP rights, passing off, patent and design non-infringement declarations, and breach of confidence claims above $250,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As a result, the High Court will have exclusive jurisdiction over: (a)	Civil infringement of copyright and all forms of registrable IP rights; (b)	Passing off actions, which are closely related to trademark infringement; (c)	Declarations of non-infringement of patents and registered designs; and (d)	Breach of confidence actions where the amount claimed exceeds $250,000.

sections.label: Specialised IP litigation track
sections.summary: MinLaw and the Supreme Court are looking into a specialised IP litigation track in the High Court with simplified processes and cost-saving features.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To ensure that parties may continue to access the Courts in a cost-effective and expeditious manner, in conjunction with the consolidation of IP disputes in the High Court, MinLaw and the Supreme Court are looking into the introduction of a specialised IP litigation "track" in the High Court, with simplified processes and also cost-saving features.

sections.label: Third party observations process
sections.summary: Clause 10 of the Bill legislates a process of third party observations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 10 of the Bill legislates a process of third party observations.

sections.label: Patent re-examination process
sections.summary: The new patent re-examination process is ex parte in nature.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new patent re-examination process is ex parte in nature.

sections.label: IP disputes arbitrable amendments
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends the Arbitration Act and clause 8 amends the International Arbitration Act to clarify that IP disputes are arbitrable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 2 amends the Arbitration Act, and clause 8 amends the International Arbitration Act, to clarify that IP disputes are capable of settlement by arbitration, in other words, that they are arbitrable.

sections.label: Registrar referral to High Court
sections.summary: Clauses 9(c), 12(c) and 20(i) give the Registrar of Patents greater flexibility to refer disputes to the High Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, clauses 9(c), 12(c) and 20(i) provide the Registrar of Patents with greater flexibility to refer disputes before the Registrar to the High Court.

sections.label: Appeals require leave of Court
sections.summary: Appeals from the relevant Registrar's decisions to the High Court can only proceed with the leave of Court where further appeals are possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Going forward, the consistent approach will be that when decisions from the relevant Registrar are appealed to the High Court, where further appeals are possible, such appeals can only proceed with the leave of Court.

sections.label: Third party observation and re-examination
sections.summary: The Bill introduces third party observation and re-examination after grant process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, this Bill introduces third party observation and re-examination after grant process.

sections.label: IP disputes in High Court
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates jurisdiction for IP disputes within the High Court, streamlining dispute resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, this Bill streamlines dispute resolutions by consolidating the jurisdiction for IP disputes within the High Court.

sections.label: IP disputes are arbitrable
sections.summary: The Bill makes clear that disputes relating to IP rights are arbitrable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Third, this Bill makes it clear that disputes relating to IP rights are arbitrable.

sections.label: Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance position
sections.summary: The Bill's position is not novel, as Hong Kong's Arbitration Ordinance made it clear from 1 January 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, the position in the Bill is not novel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is the position that is also made clear in Hong Kong by the Arbitration Ordinance which came into effect on 1 January 2018.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, citing its potential for IP owners and its three key highlights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This includes arbitrators specialising in IP, legal practitioners in the field of IP and disputes, and thought leaders in arbitration, dispute resolution and IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There is much potential in this Bill for people who develop and own IP, for instance, software engineers, designers, small medium enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Because IP rights are supported through a more robust dispute resolution structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And for those reasons, I support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill aims to ensure that the Singapore IP regime continues to support innovative activities in Singapore and positions Singapore as a choice of venue for international IP dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I see the three key highlights of the Bill as: (a) to streamline the IP dispute resolution framework in Singapore; (b) to provide certainty that IP disputes can be arbitrated in Singapore; and (c) to amend IPOS' procedures on granting and re-examining patents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I applaud the move to provide certainty that IP disputes can be arbitrated in Singapore and the arbitral award only has effect on the parties and not the world at large.

sections.label: IP disputes heard by High Court
sections.summary: In streamlining the IP dispute resolution framework, most, if not all, IP disputes will be heard by the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In streamlining the IP dispute resolution framework in Singapore, most, if not all, IP disputes will now be heard by the High Court.

sections.label: Three key Bill changes
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates most IP proceedings in the High Court, updates patent procedures, and clarifies IP disputes are arbitrable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, it consolidates the majority of IP proceedings in the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, it updates pre and post-grant patent procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, it clarifies that IP disputes are arbitrable.

sections.label: Fast-track hearing days cap
sections.summary: The Ministry proposed a two hearing day cap for fast-track cases, and questions were raised on its realism for IP disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the Ministry has proposed a cap of two hearing days for cases on the fast track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry be further studying the optimal period for hearing cases on the fast track?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I raise this because the consolidation of disputes in the High Court was motivated by the fact that the Ministry has stated that, “IP disputes often involve myriad technical details that are susceptible to repeated and extensive requests for particulars and discovery”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With this in mind, it is unclear whether a cap of two hearing days for a trial would be realistic for IP disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry has not indicated a position on whether such a trial judge for a fast-track case can grant both interim and final relief.

sections.label: Appealability of fast-track decisions
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked to clarify whether fast-track decisions are appealable and how this interacts with the two-day hearing cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third and lastly, I hope the Ministry will also clarify whether decisions from the fast track are appealable and, if so, how this will interact with the proposed two-day hearing cap.

sections.label: Specialised track and damages cap
sections.summary: Separate proceedings midway are unlikely due to upfront case management, and a $500,000 cap on damages or profits is being considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To Mr Louis Ng's point about whether separate proceedings may be filed if one determines halfway through that the "specialised" track is not suitable, that is unlikely to happen, given the upfront pre-judicial management or rather case management of the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are considering a cap of $500,000 on the value of the claim for damages or an account of profits.

sections.label: Party-and-party costs and trial cap
sections.summary: A stage-based party-and-party costs cap of $50,000 is considered, and the two-day trial cap would allow trial judge discretion to extend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are also considering a cap on party-and-party costs awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This would be stage-based, in other words, based on the stage of proceedings of the litigation, with an overall cap of $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the two-day cap for the length of trial, we propose to cap it but, at the same time, allow the trial judge discretion to extend this in the appropriate circumstances.

sections.label: Arbitration costs unaffected by amendments
sections.summary: The amendments consolidating most civil IP litigation in the High Court are not anticipated to directly impact arbitration costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As arbitration and litigation are separate and distinct methods of resolving disputes, we do not anticipate that the amendments to consolidate litigation of most civil IP disputes in the High Court will directly impact the costs of arbitration.

sections.label: Third-party patent observations
sections.summary: New section 32(1) of the Patents Act allows third parties to make observations on whether the invention is patentable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, the new section 32(1) of the Patents Act, inserted by clause 10 of the Bill, provides that third parties may make observations on the question whether the invention in the patent application is a patentable one.

sections.label: Third-party observations and examination timing
sections.summary: Third-party observations are free, and Rule 46(8)(a) requires the Examiner to issue the examination report within a fixed time period regardless of any observation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Fourth, there will be no fee to submit third-party observations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, the patent application period will not be unduly lengthened as Rule 46(8)(a) of the Patents Rules requires the Examiner to issue the examination report within a fixed time period, regardless of whether a third-party observation is made or not.

sections.label: Ownership disputes as IP rights dispute
sections.summary: Ownership disputes fall within the definition of "IP rights dispute" in the new section 52A(3) of the Arbitration Act and section 26A(4) of the International Arbitration Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ownership disputes are within the scope of "IP rights dispute", which would be defined in the new section 52A(3) of the Arbitration Act and section 26A(4) of the International Arbitration Act, inserted by clauses 2 and 8 of the Bill respectively.

sections.label: Reimbursement of first consultation fee
sections.summary: Those seeking such advice can obtain reimbursement from IPOS for the consultation fee for the first session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To assist those seeking such advice, they can obtain reimbursement from IPOS for the consultation fee for the first session.

sections.label: Amendments to Registered Designs and Trade Marks Acts
sections.summary: Clauses 28 and 34 make amendments to the Registered Designs Act and Trade Marks Act, giving IP rights owners greater assurance of enforceability and increasing patent quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Similar amendments to those – he referred to clause 6(b) which amends the Geographical Indications Act – they will also be made in this Bill at clause 28, to the Registered Designs Act, and clause 34, to the Trade Marks Act, to bring them to the same footing as what Mr Christopher de Souza referred to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And that can be found at clauses 28 and 34 respectively for the Registered Designs and the Trade Marks Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This will give IP rights owners greater assurance of the enforceability of their IP rights and also increase the overall quality of granted patents in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These reforms are part of our continual efforts to improve our IP regime to support our innovative and creative industries.
